text:
Governor Braun announces public schedule for week of Aug. 24 in Indiana
Indiana Governor Mike Braun announced on Aug. 26 his public schedule for the week of Aug. 24, outlining several key events across the state.
On Thursday, Aug. 27, Braun is scheduled to deliver opening remarks and participate in the groundbreaking ceremony for the SK Hynix Advanced Packaging and Research & Development Hub at Holloway Gymnasium in West Lafayette. The event is intended to highlight Indiana's role in next-generation technology innovation and global economic advancement.
Later that day, Braun will hold a briefing at the State Emergency Operations Center in Indianapolis following the approval of a major disaster declaration for 21 Indiana counties. He will be joined by Jonathan Whitham, Executive Director of the Indiana Department of Homeland Security.
Also on Thursday, Braun will attend a ribbon-cutting ceremony marking the completion of Rolls-Royce’s decade-long $1 billion modernization project at its Indianapolis facility. According to information provided by his office, Rolls-Royce has invested over $1 billion in modernizing and expanding operations in Indiana, supporting approximately 3,500 direct employees engaged in advanced manufacturing and engineering roles.
On Saturday, Aug. 29, Braun will deliver remarks at The National Guard Association of the United States National Conference & Exhibition at the Indiana Convention Center in Indianapolis. The conference is expected to bring together around 3,500 Soldiers and Airmen from all states and territories as well as government officials and Pentagon leaders.
Braun’s background includes service on school boards and as a state representative; he won election to the U.S. Senate in 2018 before becoming governor; he grew his company into a national entity employing thousands; championed over forty bills that became law during his Senate term; graduated summa cum laude with an economics degree from Wabash College; earned an MBA from Harvard Business School; has been married for forty-nine years; and raised four children, according to the official website.
